detail.en: The whole song, every part together

detail.en: Follow the words as it plays

text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
H. W. Petrie wrote this song in 1897 for a baritone or bass voice, which is why here the bass, not the soprano, sings the tune.

source.en: "Asleep in the Deep" (New York: F. A. Mills), Lester S. Levy Sheet Music Collection, Johns Hopkins University, Box 145, Item 046, read from the scan

The whole song, with the guide.
Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
Once more on your own, from the top.
Record the tune of Asleep in the Deep in Sing, with the other parts playing.
The last line keeps its lowest notes for the end: "Beware!" is sung twice, the second falling a whole octave, before the bass sinks to "asleep in the deep".
